links.outcome: Concordance of AI pharmacological recommendations with guideline and systematic-review evidence for chronic pain
links.effect: Full concordance in 38.5% of cases, partial concordance in 53.8%, no concordance in 7.7%; tDCS parameter recommendations varied, especially electrode montage and session standardization.
links.quote: Regarding pharmacological management, full concordance between AI-generated recommendations and evidence-based standards was observed in 38.5% of cases, partial concordance in 53.8%, and no concordance in 7.7%.

screen.reason: Empirically evaluates the concordance of LLM-generated clinical recommendations (ChatGPT and OpenEvidence) against evidence-based standards for chronic pain management, but does not test a specific deployment safeguard or practice.
